_comment: Game Review 2.0 findability constants. Refitting rewrites this file, never code. The visibility weights and the calibration below are FITTED (Phase 3); the tau / gate / alternate constants are still the spec's placeholders.
_score_mode_comment: MEASURED. 'calibrated' = visibility reweight + Elo-shaped calibration, and it is what ships. Against 272 rated Lichess puzzles (train) and an independent 320 (holdout), |r(score, puzzle rating)| goes 0.23 -> 0.38 versus the previous 'mean_ca', and the line probability tracks the Elo expectancy at MAE 0.170 / r 0.741 on the holdout. 'mean_ca' and 'rfind' are kept for the calibration harness; both use the old calc reweight.

tau_volatility._comment: Phase 4: tau = f(volatility). enabled=false keeps constant tau.

visibility._comment: FITTED. Replaces the calc term for the shipped score. The old calc leaned on dep (iterative-deepening depth) and narr, but the review reuses the volatility pass's MultiPV, so d_star is 1 for every move and narr is 0 — the reweight reallocated nothing, and supplying the real values changed |r| by 0.004. Measured against puzzle rating, d_star and narr have spearman 0.00; the move giving check has -0.41, the move being quiet +0.32, PV forcingness -0.30. Rejected after measuring: the move hanging itself (-0.12, and the wrong sign for a difficulty term), backward moves (-0.04), edge squares (-0.03), PV length (+0.01).

calibration._comment: FITTED. Each grid rating implies a difficulty D_r = r - 173.7*logit(C_A(r)); D is their mean, and the calibrated curve is the Elo expectancy for D. c0/c1 are the residual correction, fitted so the product over a puzzle's whole solution line reproduces 1/(1+10^((rating-r)/400)). They land at 0 and 1.028 — the reweighted curve is already on the Lichess rating scale to within 3%. An unconstrained affine map in logit space fitted the puzzles slightly better but extrapolated the wrong way onto easy positions it had never seen (it scored a wide-open game position 61 where the raw model said 79), which is why the Elo shape is used instead.

_rating_grid_comment: MEASURED, do not widen. Maia-3 conditions on raw Elo 600-2600 and the obvious move was to widen the grid to match. Against 72 stratified Lichess puzzles (seed 7, line mode, Maia-3) the score gets *worse* as the grid widens: |r(score, puzzle rating)| = 0.603 at 1100-2000, 0.594 at 1000-2200, 0.591 at 900-2300, 0.577 at 600-2600, and 0.602 at 1200-1950. Averaging over ratings nobody in the sample plays at compresses easy and hard positions together.
_bands_comment: MEASURED against the calibrated scale, where the score is a probability: the share of players across the 1100-2000 grid who find an acceptable move. Thresholds are the readings of that probability, and they land near the quintiles of 286 real game positions (21% engine-only, 22% hard, 22% needs thought, 17% natural, 17% obvious). The old 90/70/45/20 cut-offs were set before the score meant anything and put 74% of rated puzzles in Hard or Engine-only with nothing ever reaching Natural.
